launch_app.description: Launch an installed channel by app id. Ids come from the Installed Apps query; the Channel entity below joins the two. Launching is NOT gated by "Control by mobile apps" on the observed fleet — the gate lists keypress/keydown/keyup, icon and the tv-channel queries.

app_id.description: The id attribute of an <app> element from /query/apps, e.g. "12" for Netflix. Numeric today, but the doc calls it an id, not a number — treat it as an opaque string.

press_backspace.description: Delete the character left of the cursor in the focused field.

press_channel_down.description: Previous tuner channel (Roku TV, tuner input).

press_channel_up.description: Next tuner channel (Roku TV, tuner input).

press_find_remote.description: Make the paired remote chirp, on hardware whose remote supports being found. Other devices answer 200 and do nothing.

press_fwd.description: Fast-forward; press repeatedly for faster speeds.

press_home.description: Return to the home screen. Also wakes the display from screensaver.

press_info.description: The * key: options for the focused item.

press_input_av1.description: Switch a Roku TV to the composite (AV) input.

press_input_hdmi1.description: Switch a Roku TV to HDMI 1.

press_input_hdmi2.description: Switch a Roku TV to HDMI 2.

press_input_hdmi3.description: Switch a Roku TV to HDMI 3.

press_input_hdmi4.description: Switch a Roku TV to HDMI 4.

press_input_tuner.description: Switch a Roku TV to the antenna/tuner input.

press_instant_replay.description: Jump back a few seconds in playback (the replay key).

press_play.description: Play/pause toggle — one key serves both.

press_power_off.description: Put a Roku TV into standby.

press_power_on.description: Wake a Roku TV from standby.

press_rev.description: Rewind; press repeatedly for faster speeds.

type_char.description: Type one character into the focused field — the Lit_ key form from ecp_common.request_format.escaping. Any UTF-8 character rides percent-encoded after the literal Lit_ prefix; the renderer does the encoding, the caller passes the bare character.

device.name: Roku External Control Protocol
device.notes: Roku ECP is a local REST-style HTTP API exposed on port 8060 with no authentication. Discovery is two-step: SSDP M-SEARCH for roku:ecp returns a LOCATION such as http://<ip>:8060/, then consumers must fetch http://<ip>:8060/query/device-info to get XML identity. The same discovered host:8060 is used for /query/*, /keypress/*, /launch/*, and /input endpoints. AirPlay mDNS can also locate compatible TCL Roku TVs but ECP identity comes from /query/device-info. Since Roku OS 14.1 the keypress/keydown/keyup, query/icon, query/tv-channels and query/tv-active-channel commands additionally require Settings > System > Advanced system settings > "Control by mobile apps" = Enabled; query endpoints such as device-info remain open.

openness.notes: Roku publishes ECP and encourages third-party clients, which makes this one of the registry's rare documented_api entries. reverse_engineered is still true because the published surface is partial: /query/apps and /query/active-app were dropped from the current doc's command table yet remain live on the observed OS 15.2.4 fleet, and the OS 14.1 "Control by mobile apps" gate below is recorded from community reports and live behaviour, not from the ECP document.

credentials.notes: ECP has no authentication at all. Anything that can route to port 8060 can drive the device, so treat network reachability as the entire access control model. Since Roku OS 14.1 there is also a universal on-device gate: Settings > System > Advanced system settings > "Control by mobile apps" must be Enabled or keypress/keydown/keyup, query/icon, query/tv-channels and query/tv-active-channel are rejected.

factory_reset.effect: Clears network credentials, account link, installed channels and settings; the device returns to first-run setup.

procedures.indicator: Device reboots into the first-run wizard.

steps.notes: Use this when the screen is unusable; the menu path is preferred otherwise.

methods.description: Guided first-run setup on the TV/player: language, network selection, passphrase entry with the on-screen keyboard, then a software update and (optionally) an account link. The account link gates channel installs, not ECP.

steps.action: Power on the device and follow the on-screen setup with the remote.
Select the WiFi network and enter the passphrase on the device itself.

steps.action: Confirm ECP is reachable from the LAN.

setup.notes: Roku onboarding happens entirely on the device's own screen with the remote; there is no app-driven provisioning protocol to reimplement. ECP itself needs no pairing — it is open to every host on the LAN once the device is online, which is a discovery convenience and a security liability at the same time.

rejoin.notes: Settings > Network > Set up connection re-runs only the network step. A factory reset is never needed just to change routers.

entities.notes: TV-class keys. turn_off is discrete and safe to send blind; turn_on works only from the warm standby PowerOff leaves behind ("Fast TV Start" keeps it warm) — a cold set needs the physical remote. No power state is readable over ECP.

entities.notes: TV-class key; see commands.press_power_on for the standby caveat.

entities.name: Options
entities.notes: The * key. Named Options because that is what it does; Info is the wire spelling.

entities.name: Channel Up
entities.notes: TV-class key; meaningful on the tuner input.

entities.name: Channel Down
entities.notes: TV-class key; meaningful on the tuner input.

entities.name: Keyboard
entities.notes: Types into whatever field has focus — the entity cannot know which, and neither can the device tell it. Gated by "Control by mobile apps" like every keypress.

entities.name: Channel
entities.notes: Roku's own UI calls these channels, so the entity does too. On the home screen the Active App element has no id attribute — the current selection is then simply none of the options, which is the honest answer. Launching a channel that is already foreground restarts or resumes it, per the device.

limited_mode_probe.apk_teardown: Static analysis of the official Roku app: in Limited mode it rides "ECP2", an authenticated WebSocket session on the same port 8060. The teardown plus a live re-implementation against this fleet the same day showed the session accepts client-id auth whose secret ships in the app — no Roku account needed — and that query-apps and key-press both answer 200 over it on a Limited-mode TV. The full protocol is the top-level `ecp2` block. A line-by-line re-audit of the app's code on 2026-08-13 confirmed every ECP2 mechanism that block records: the client-id secret's encoded UUID, its nibble transform and the SHA-1 + Base64 response construction (the app's client-id challenge strategy), port 8060, the roku:ecp SSDP search target, the ecp-2 WebSocket subprotocol with the Android origin header on /ecp-session, the v1/ecp/token?assert=true JWT endpoint and its ecp2_jwt.enabled remote-config gate, and the app's 55-entry request-type table.

results.observed: 400 and 403 "ECP command not allowed in Limited mode."

limited_mode_probe.setting: Settings > System > Advanced system settings > Control by mobile apps = Limited

http_endpoints.description: XML device identity, model, user display name, serial, device-id, network type, and software version. Roku OS 15.0 adds supports-tv-power-control and supports-audio-volume-control on streaming players.

http_endpoints.description: XML list of installed Roku channels and launchable app IDs. Dropped from the current official ECP doc's command table but still live on-device (used by python-rokuecp / Home Assistant). One <app> element per channel: the id attribute is what /launch/{app_id} takes, and the element text is the display name. Open while "Control by mobile apps" is Permissive, but REFUSED in its middle "Limited" position — observed 2026-08-11 as 400 and 403 spellings of "ECP command not allowed in Limited mode." (ecp_common.response_format.gating.limited_mode).
http_endpoints.name: Installed Apps

  <app id="837" subtype="ndka" type="appl" version="1.0.80">YouTube</app>

</apps>

http_endpoints.description: Current foreground app and active media context. Dropped from the current official ECP doc's command table but still live on-device, and confirmed open even in the "Limited" control-by-mobile-apps position (observed 2026-08-11: 200 while /query/apps on the same TV refused). The <app> element matches the Installed Apps shape — except on the home screen and in the screensaver, where it carries no id attribute at all (the text is just "Roku"): a consumer matching the current channel by id must treat a missing attribute as "none of them", not as an error.
http_endpoints.name: Active App

http_endpoints.description: Playback state, position, duration, and media metadata when available. Refused (403) in the "Limited" control-by-mobile-apps position on the observed fleet, 2026-08-11.
http_endpoints.name: Media Player

http_endpoints.description: Press and release one remote key. The full key vocabulary, from the official ECP doc: Home, Rev, Fwd, Play, Select, Left, Right, Down, Up, Back, InstantReplay, Info, Backspace, Search, Enter, FindRemote on every device; VolumeUp, VolumeDown, VolumeMute, PowerOn, PowerOff, ChannelUp, ChannelDown, InputTuner, InputHDMI1-InputHDMI4, InputAV1 on Roku TVs; and Lit_<percent-encoded char> for literal text (ecp_common.request_format.escaping). The `commands` block below names one invocation per key so entities have something to bind. Since Roku OS 14.1 this endpoint requires Settings > System > Advanced system settings > "Control by mobile apps" = Enabled.
http_endpoints.name: Keypress

http_endpoints.description: Press and hold a key from the same vocabulary as Keypress; pair with Keyup to release. What a long-press on a remote button sends. Gated by "Control by mobile apps" exactly as Keypress is.

http_endpoints.description: Release a key held by Keydown. Gated like Keypress.
http_endpoints.name: Keyup

http_endpoints.name: TV Active Channel

http_endpoints.name: Launch App

http_endpoints.description: SUNSET: Roku removed the search ECP command as of Roku OS 12.0 (notice in the official ECP doc). It worked on firmware 7.5-11.x only and is gone on the observed OS 15.2.4 fleet; retained here for older firmware.
http_endpoints.name: Search Browse

http_endpoints.description: Query-string sensor/custom-input channel forwarded to the running app (e.g. POST /input?acceleration.x=0.0&acceleration.y=0.0), per the official ECP doc. It takes no {source} path segment and does NOT switch TV inputs — input switching is POST /keypress/InputHDMI1..4, InputTuner, or InputAV1.
http_endpoints.name: Custom Input

auth.description: On connect the device sends {"notify": "authenticate", "param-challenge": "<base64>", "param-methods": [...]}. Two methods were offered by every fleet TV: "jwt" — a token from https://auth.prod.mobile.roku.com/v1/ecp/token?assert=true tied to the signed-in Roku account, gated in the app by the remote-config flag ecp2_jwt.enabled, which defaults off — and "client-id", which needs NO account: answer {"request": "authenticate", "request-id": "1", "param-response": base64(SHA-1(challenge + secret))}. The secret is the app's own client id, shipped in the APK (the client-id challenge strategy): the UUID 95E610D0-7C29-44EF-FB0F-97F1FCE4C297 with every hex nibble n replaced by (24 - n) & 15, i.e. F3A278B8-1C6F-44A9-9D89-F1979CA4C6F1. A successful answer gets {"response": "authenticate", "status": "200"} and the session then accepts the full vocabulary — in Limited mode included. Client-id is also the app's own fallback: when a jwt answer fails, the app retries the same challenge with client-id automatically.

jwt_response_format.confidence_notes: Read from the app's JWT challenge-response strategy but never exercised against hardware: the fleet session authenticated with client-id, and the ecp2_jwt.enabled flag gates the jwt path off by default, so this construction is app-derived only.
jwt_response_format.description: The jwt method's on-wire param-response: the literal prefix "JWT:" followed by base64 of the token bytes XORed byte-wise with the decoded challenge and the device ESN — token and ESN taken as US-ASCII, the challenge base64-decoded, and challenge and ESN repeated cyclically over the token length.

ecp2.framing: JSON text frames. A client request is {"request": "<name>", "request-id": "<n>", ...params}; the device answers {"response": "<name>", "response-id": "<n>", "status": "200", ...} with any payload base64 in content-data beside a content-type, and sends unsolicited notices with "notify" in place of "response". The request names are the ECP paths dashed: query-apps, query-active-app, query-device-info, key-press/key-down/key-up (param-key), launch, input, query-tv-channels-ex, query-icon, set-textedit-text (whole-string text entry — no per-character Lit_ loop needed), and more: the app's request-type table holds 55 entries in all, running from av-sync queries to picture settings.
ecp2.notes: Whether using a competitor-shaped client id is acceptable is a policy question for a consumer of this spec, not a technical one; the mechanism itself is documented here because it is how the protocol works. Roku can rotate or revoke the id in a firmware update at any time, so a client should treat ECP2 as an enhancement over plain ECP with fallback, never the only path. Consumers may treat this block's presence in a spec as the signed-session capability signal: a device spec carrying `ecp2` supports the authenticated WebSocket session, and one without it is plain-ECP only.

request_format.description: Requests go to http://<ip>:8060<path>, where <ip> comes from SSDP discovery (the LOCATION header is http://<ip>:8060/). Command POSTs carry an EMPTY body: no Content-Type, no payload, no SOAPACTION — the path is the entire instruction. No authentication exists at any firmware level; see device.setup.credentials.
request_format.escaping: Literal text entry uses the Lit_ key form: POST /keypress/Lit_a types 'a', and any UTF-8 character rides percent-encoded after the prefix — /keypress/Lit_%20 is a space. Only the character is percent-encoded; the Lit_ prefix itself is literal.

http.headers: None required. The device applies its own Host-header sanity check (requests must come from a private/LAN address); a client on the same network sends nothing special to pass it.

response_format.description: Command endpoints answer 200 OK with an empty body on success; query endpoints answer XML. A 403 Forbidden means the "Control by mobile apps" gate below is closed — surface that as "enable control on the TV", not as a network failure.

gating.description: The gate does NOT split along command/query lines, which is the trap: it covers the three key endpoints plus three of the queries, and leaves launching and the identity/app queries open. So a client must not suppress the whole control surface on one 403, nor assume a query cannot return one. The lists below name `http_endpoints` entries, so a consumer filters on data rather than parsing this paragraph.
gating.limited_mode: Live correction, probed 2026-08-11 against the OS 15.2.4 fleet (evidence.limited_mode_probe): with "Control by mobile apps" set to the middle "Limited" position, the refusal is BROADER than the gate notice suggests. /query/apps answered "ECP command not allowed in Limited mode." — as HTTP 400 on Living Room TV and HTTP 403 on Kitchen TV and Spare TV, and the same TV switched between the two spellings within minutes — and /query/media-player answered 403, while /query/device-info and /query/active-app kept answering 200 and every keypress answered 403. So a client must treat 400-with-that-body as the same refusal 403 means, must NOT assume query endpoints are exempt, and must expect the channel list to be unreadable over plain ECP until the setting is raised to Permissive — OR switch to ECP2, the authenticated WebSocket session documented in the `ecp2` block below, which Limited mode does not refuse.
gating.open_notes: The gate notice enumerates what it covers, so `open` is everything else — that is the rule these lists follow, not a per-endpoint observation. Launching is open on the observed OS 15.2.4 fleet, which is what makes a channel launcher work on a TV whose remote keys are all refused, and the identity and app queries being open is what lets that launcher build its list at all. Custom Input is open by the same enumeration rule but is the one entry here this project has not exercised: it forwards to whatever app is running, so there is no reply that distinguishes "delivered" from "ignored".
gating.setting: Settings > System > Advanced system settings > "Control by mobile apps", introduced in Roku OS 14.1.
